title: Dynamics 365 Business Central: How to quickly identify the first transaction date and the number of days since the last sale with a customer
summary: The Customer Statistics page (Customer > Statistics, then Show more) shows a customer's first transaction date and the days since the last sale without any code. First Transaction Date is a standard field on table 18 Customer, while Days Since Last Sale is only a variable on page 151, so the post gives a page extension that adds both to the Customer List.
key_points: Open Customer > Statistics from the Customer List or Card and choose Show more; Customer Since and Lifetime (since) show the first transaction date
The Days Since Last Sale value on the statistics page counts days since the customer's last purchase
First Transaction Date is a standard field on the Customer table; DaysSinceLastSale is a page variable, not a table field

A sample page extension adds both to the Customer List, computing days as work date minus the posting date of the latest non-reversed customer ledger entry with positive sales, with drill-down to that entry

quotes.text: You don't need complex customizations to gain deeper customer insights.
quotes.why_it_matters: Establishes that standard Business Central functionality meets customer analysis needs without development effort

quotes.text: The First Transaction Date field is a standard field in table 18 Customer.
quotes.why_it_matters: Confirms the field exists natively, enabling reuse across pages without custom coding
